question: Who gives a fleet whose file names a base with no naval base the base the save has.

slots_noted.0x1D01B0: Already recorded; this revises the comment only.
slots_noted.0x1B80D0: Already recorded; this revises the comment only.
slots_noted.0x1CF6A0: Already recorded; this revises the comment only.

addresses.name: CNavy::CheckBase
addresses.comment:
**CNavy slot 18, the last step of a fleet's hour.** Nothing while the fleet's base is held by no enemy of its country. Otherwise the fleet is taken off that base and given the nearest by sea (CMapProvince::NavalDistanceTo from the province it is in) of its country's naval bases, then of its faction's members'; with none, and no port left to its country (total_num_of_ports), it is queued for removal. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-seaair.md, section 3.

**Read whole on the listing and run 2026-11-19** (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 150). It also runs as a unit block closes: CUnit::AfterLoad calls it (from 0x5B8163), so a fleet the loader left with no base gets one before the first day. A null base (+0x98) skips the enemy test and goes straight on. The base is zeroed (0x5D025E), then each node of the owner's NavalBases (CCountry +0xD80, province-number order on a new game) is measured with CMapProvince::NavalDistanceTo(the base province, out, the fleet's location id +0x130 -> +0xD0) and taken where strictly below the running best, which starts at 999,999,000 (0x3B9AC618); the base stored is the province's +0x58, its naval base object. With none, the faction's members (faction +0x28, its node list) and each one's NavalBases the same way, the best starting at 1,410,000,920 (0x540BE018). NavalDistanceTo answers 0 where either province has no sea index, so from a coast with no port every base measures 0 and the first of the list wins - BlackICE's French fleet at Djibouti (9867) is given Guadeloupe (485), as the start save has it. With none at all and total_num_of_ports (+0x1060) 0 it is queued for removal.
addresses.evidence: The listing at VA 0x5D01B0-0x5D03B3 and 0x5CF82A-0x5CF856; probes/hoinavybase.lua on a BlackICE GitHub new game as Ireland, 2026-11-19: the fleet's +0x98 written at 0x5D025E (0) and 0x5D02BF (Guadeloupe's naval base object), the return address 0x5B8163 on the stack, and the base unchanged at the head of day 1.

addresses.name: CUnit::AfterLoad
addresses.comment:
**CPersistent slot 5, and where a unit's id comes from.** If the block carried an id (either half of the pair at +8 non-zero) it keeps it and then pushes the global generator at 0x170AF78 past it, so a later runtime id cannot collide with it. If it carried none, it takes `counter++` and stamps id type **0x29 (41)**. That is why an OOB file need not carry ids at all. **Then, where the unit has a province (+0x130): CUnit::RebuildDefinition(unit, 1), `loading` (+0x48) cleared, CUnit::RebuildAvatar, CUnit::EnterProvince(its own province again), and slot 18** - nothing for a CArmy (the empty stub), CNavy::CheckBase for a fleet, CAir::CheckBase for an air unit. `this` is the CPersistent subobject, CUnit + 8.

**It ends a unit's load with the unit's slot 18** (the call returning to 0x5B8163) - CNavy::CheckBase for a fleet, CAir::CheckBase for an air unit - so a fleet or an air unit is given a base as its block closes: an order of battle's, load_oob's or a save's. Seen in the running game 2026-11-19 (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 150).

addresses.name: CNavy::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CNavy::LoadKey(CNavy* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment:
What a `navy` block adds over CUnit::LoadKey; **`this` is the CPersistent subobject, CNavy + 8**. `at_sea` (0x3FC) is read into this+0x2F0, which is **CNavy +0x2F8, the post-battle wait** - not +0x2F0, so it never touches the carrying list's lock byte. `base` sets the home base through CUnit::SetBase where the province has a naval base (else logs 'can not find NAVAL base'). **`army`, `theatre`, `armygroup`, `corps` and `division`** each build a CArmy (new 0x308, ctor 0x4828C0): byte +0x48 set, oob_level from the key (0x5B8C70), slot 28 with the fleet's +0x160, the fleet's owner (0x5BC460), the block read by the unit's Load; where it then has a location it goes aboard - CNavy::AddCarried(the fleet, it), which **zeroes the dig_in and staging_province just read** and keeps `target` - and into its owner's unit list (CCountry::AddUnit); without a location it is deleted. Its `parent` is restored later, by CUnit_RelinkLoadedParent as the game is entered. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-oob.md and FINDINGS-transport.md, section A.7.

The base key's test is the province's naval base shortcut (+0x300) -> level_max (+0x20) above 0 (0x5CF848-0x5CF856); a province failing it leaves the fleet with no base until CUnit::AfterLoad's CNavy::CheckBase gives one (FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 150).
